title: Tiered Commit Bucket Simulator and Recommendations
body:
Summary:
This is a working simulator and recommendation draft for a tiered GPU commit model (bucketed commitments + burst pool). Purpose: provide a concrete math-first model to translate customer committed hours into blended unit economics, and to produce operational guidance for sizing Dedicated capacity pools.

High-level proposal (one-liner):
- Offer 3 commitment tiers (Core, Flex, Burst) with separate pricing and guarantees. Core = reserved, predictable throughput; Flex = discounted but preemptible-like scheduling; Burst = pay-as-you-go add-on for peaks.

Key assumptions (editable inputs):
- GPU types considered: A100-80GB, A100-40GB, A10G, T4 (short names: A100-80, A100-40, A10G, T4)
- Baseline hourly infra costs (fully loaded): A100-80 = $3.60/hr; A100-40 = $2.40/hr; A10G = $1.10/hr; T4 = $0.45/hr
- Average platform overhead (scheduling, storage, networking) = 12% of infra cost
- Target baseline utilization for Core = 80% (we expect customers to use 80% of committed capacity on average)
- Flex effective utilization assumption = Core customers will shift 10–30% to Flex when they need burst elasticity
- Burst pool priced at ~1.6x the core hourly (premium for capacity on demand)

Sheet tabs (text representation):
1) Inputs (single-row key=value editable)
- commitment_months=12
- core_commit_hours_per_month=720 (1 GPU reserved full month)
- planned_headroom=10%
- expected_monthly_hours_used_per_core=576 (80%)
- flex_discount_vs_core=25%
- burst_premium_vs_core=60%
- operational_buffer_hours=48

2) Cost Model (per GPU type)
Columns: GPU, base_hr, platform_overhead_pct, total_hr_cost, core_price_pct_of_cost, core_price_hr, flex_price_hr, burst_price_hr
Example rows (calculated):
A100-80, 3.60, 12%, 4.03, 120%, 4.84, 3.63, 7.74
A100-40, 2.40, 12%, 2.69, 120%, 3.23, 2.42, 4.86
A10G, 1.10, 12%, 1.23, 120%, 1.48, 1.11, 1.97
T4, 0.45, 12%, 0.50, 120%, 0.60, 0.45, 0.96
Notes on pricing multipliers: core_price_pct_of_cost default set to 120% (margin + fixed infra amortization). Flex price = core * (1 - flex_discount_vs_core). Burst price = core * (1 + burst_premium_vs_core).

3) Utilization Forecast (3 scenarios)
- Scenario A (Conservative): average utilization per committed GPU = 65% monthly; burst demand 5% of total hours.
- Scenario B (Baseline): utilization = 80%; burst demand 15% of hours.
- Scenario C (Aggressive): utilization = 92%; burst demand 28% of hours.

Table example (per 100 committed GPUs, A100-40 base):
Scenario, committed_gpus, committed_hours_total, expected_used_hours, idle_hours, burst_hours_needed
Conservative, 100, 72000, 46800, 25200, 3600
Baseline, 100, 72000, 57600, 14400, 10800
Aggressive, 100, 72000, 66240, 5760, 20160

4) Blended Revenue & Unit Cost (per scenario)
- Calculate: revenue_core = core_price_hr * used_hours_on_core; revenue_flex = flex_price_hr * used_hours_on_flex; revenue_burst = burst_price_hr * burst_hours
- Unit cost = (infra_cost_total + platform_overhead_total) / total_used_hours (include idle charge allocation per commitments)
- Blended margin = revenue_total - infra_cost_total - op_costs

Example baseline math (A100-40, 100 GPUs):
- infra_cost_total = base_hr * committed_hours_total = 2.40 * 72,000 = $172,800
- overhead = 12% * infra_cost_total = $20,736
- total_cost = 193,536
- used_core_hours (assume 80% used on core) = 57,600
- assume 15% of used hours run on burst/flex mix: flex_used = 6,000, burst_used = 8,100 (example split)
- revenue_core = 3.23 * 51,600 = $166,668 (note: 51,600 is used hours staying on core after flex/burst shift)
- revenue_flex = 2.42 * 6,000 = $14,520
- revenue_burst = 4.86 * 8,100 = $39,366
- revenue_total = $220,554
- blended_unit_revenue = revenue_total / total_used_hours (57,600+6,000+8,100) = ~ $2.83/hr
- blended_unit_cost = total_cost / (total_used_hours + idle_hours_allocated?) = 193,536 / 72,000 = $2.69/hr (when amortized across committed hours)
- blended_margin = revenue_total - total_cost = $26,018 (~12%)

5) Sensitivity grid (manual table):
Dimensions: utilization (x-axis: 60%,70%,80%,90%), flex_discount (y-axis: 10%,20%,30%) -> compute blended_margin percent.
Quick insight (toy numbers): at 70% util and 30% flex discount margin drops below 6%; at 90% util and 10% flex discount margin >18%.

Operational recommendations (draft):
- Offer a labeled product with three guarantees: Core (SLA-backed latency and reserved throughput), Flex (discounted, best-effort preemption window), Burst (on-demand high-price pool).
- Commit sizing guidance: sell Core in 4-week blocks (min 0.25 GPU) but recommend annualized commits for larger discounts. Provide customers with a simple simulator UI that takes their peak/tail distribution and outputs recommended mix (Core:Flex:Burst).
- Autoscaling policy: keep elastic headroom = max(planned_headroom, 2 * standard_deviation of hourly demand). For customers with spiky diurnal patterns, suggest >20% Flex allocation.
- Idle mitigation: convert long-term idle capacity to temporary Flex availability in the next billing period (soft rollovers) instead of fully refunding; use an incentive credit to discourage over-commit at >month granularity.

Pricing engineering rules (practical):
- Core price should be set to at least 1.2x total_hr_cost to cover margin and amortization; special enterprise deals can go down to 1.05x with minimum guaranteed volumes and longer commits.
- Flex discount should be configurable per-customer depending on historical utilization; default 20-25% works across mid-market.
- Burst premium should be at least 50% to discourage constant reliance but remain cheaper than 2x core to be usable.

Implementation checklist (next steps):
- Convert this sheet into a live Google Sheet with parameter cells and scenario dropdowns (owner: Ravi; due: 2026-03-20).
- Add hourly real-customer telemetry import to simulate historical fit (owner: Eng-Observability; ticket: JIRA-PRJ-4123).
- UX: build a simple commit sizing modal in Redwood Console that runs this model live for customers (owner: Product Console; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/298).

Open questions / risk items:
- How to treat GPU family heterogeneity in blended pricing when customers mix A100 and A10G within a pool? (current workaround: price-per-gpu-class bands and let customers pin to family).
- Spot/preemptible availability risk: how much buffer should we assume for Flex? recommended to model 10-25% preemption allowance by default.
- Tax and region variance: need to include region multipliers per cloud region (EMEA/APAC premiums).

Appendix: quick formulas and cell references (for when this is ported to a sheet)
- total_hr_cost = base_hr * (1 + platform_overhead_pct)
- core_price_hr = total_hr_cost * core_price_pct_of_cost
- flex_price_hr = core_price_hr * (1 - flex_discount_vs_core)
- burst_price_hr = core_price_hr * (1 + burst_premium_vs_core)
- infra_cost_total = base_hr * committed_hours_total (sum across GPU classes)
- blended_unit_cost = infra_cost_total / committed_hours_total

Reflection note (why different from other docs):
- This doc purposely models a 3-bucket approach (Core/Flex/Burst) and emphasizes operational rules and UX hooks for the Console simulator rather than the pure commit economics matrices; it includes sample per-100-GPU walkthroughs and explicit implementation tasks.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Create Google Sheet from this text and add scenario toggle (Ravi)
- [ ] Add telemetry ingestion PR and sample customer data (Eng-Observability)
- [ ] Sync with Legal on enterprise minimums and contract language (Cust-Success)

End of draft.
